messages.author: 082ede990d64de46
messages.subject: Distance script
parts:
Hi there, Does anyone have a script they could share that could be used to
simulate DISTANCE detection from a known population distribution? What I
have in mind is being able to set up transects across the population in a
GIS and get all the distances to objects (plants in this case) from the
transect line within a truncated width and then be able to apply a detection
function to come up with something that simulates field detectability.

Thanks

messages.author: 6de9a0534fa1c61b
messages.subject: Re: Distance script
parts:
Dear Colin and others,
we are presently working along the same lines. A student of mine is
programming a model where you can import your real GIS landscape, ideal
transects, and real transects. The idea is to put in various known
population that have:
- variable amounts of clumping (e.g. from random to very clmped)
- and a range of cluster sizes that equals the observed ditsribution

Additionally, there will also be the possibility to vary the probability of
detection based on the distance to the transect and to allow movement of the
animals during the survey. The output of each simulation will look like the
output of a real survey.

My original idea was to feed this simulated data back into program DISTANCE.
However, the program is obviously not made to process 1000 repications :)
So I would appreshiate any help with implementing the math behind DISTANCE
into the simulation model.

The aim is to have a model running and analysis for our study area in
Mongolia within the next 6-9 months. The model could be a nice tool to help
with field design in other areas as well.

I would appreshiate an comments or advise on our modelling approach.
Thanks,
Petra Kaczensky

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Distance script
parts:
Hi Petra, Colin, list:

First: We (Distance development team) would like to implement spatially
explicit simulations of distance sampling surveys on animal populations
in the Distance software, and indeed have a grant proposal submitted at
present that would provide funding to do this. Distance can already
work with GIS data, and can already simulate surveys based on input
design criteria. What is needed is an interface and engine to generate
animal populations and something to simulate the process of observing
the animals given the transect lines. If you already have a competent
programmer working on this, then we'd be very happy to collaborate and
perhaps you could get something that can work within Distance. Perhaps
we can discuss this off the list.

Second: The WiSP library for R is already capable of simulating animal
populations (in quite complex spatial configurations) and distance
sampling (as well as other types of) surveys on these populations. The
limitation is that it can only cope with rather simple study areas
(rectangles) and survey designs. For more info, see
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/estimating.abundance/WiSP/index.html

Third: The analysis engines in Distance *are* set up to process 1000
replications or more. You can call them easily from outside of the
Distance interface. The CDS/MCDS engine is a FORTRAN program, and the
new MRDS engine is an R library. An example of calling the MCDS engine
from outside of the Distance interface is given by Eric Rexstad in the
following tech report
http://eprints.st-andrews.ac.uk/archive/00000447/
I have also previously posted on this list about various other options,
and there is something about this in the Distance online manual (MCDS
appendix). There is a small Visual Basic 6 project on the Support page
of the Distance web pages that demonstrates calling the Distance 4
version of the CDS engine from VB. I can update this to Distance 5 if
that would be useful. Bottom line is: I would not recommend
re-implementing the analysis capabilities of Distance in some other
software as part of your simulations -- instead, call what's there!

Hope some of this is some use. Cheers,

- Len Thomas
